title: Workspace Heartbeat Secure MCP Tunnel & Bandwidth v1
goal: Preserve the accepted Workspace Heartbeat executor-liveness UX, including the approximately one-second live-card freshness poll and silent executor-touch signal, while removing the free-ngrok bandwidth/availability dependency. Measure the actual Heartbeat traffic path and payload costs, migrate ChatGPT-to-Lambda MCP transport to OpenAI Secure MCP Tunnel if the supported product path satisfies the security and capacity requirements, minimize unnecessary bytes without weakening liveness semantics, and retire the public ngrok endpoint only after an isolated and reversible live acceptance.
acceptance_criteria: Recover and verify the exact current Heartbeat source/runtime, launcher, MCP endpoint, live-card polling path, and existing rollback state before changing transport.

Treat the October 2026 ngrok incident as an infrastructure-availability failure: ERR_NGROK_725 after approximately 1.02 GB of 1 GB monthly data-transfer allowance; do not change Heartbeat semantics merely to work around the exhausted free tunnel.

Measure or deterministically estimate request frequency, response size, headers/protocol overhead where observable, and which path is responsible for the one-second live-card executor-signal polling before attributing the bandwidth incident.
Preserve the current operator UX in which executor freshness can update independently of semantic progress and the card/server poll can remain approximately one second.

Preserve heartbeat_begin_turn, heartbeat_update, heartbeat_touch, heartbeat_get, task/turn ownership, semantic history, turn isolation, grow-through-five/scroll-from-six UI behavior, and the accepted executor-touch emission policy unless a separately reviewed change is explicitly required.

Prefer an outbound-only OpenAI Secure MCP Tunnel path so the Lambda host does not require a public inbound Heartbeat endpoint; verify the actual supported setup and applicable request/payload/session limits from current OpenAI documentation before cutover.

If Secure MCP Tunnel is not available or does not satisfy the requirements, stop at a documented blocker rather than exposing a broad public Lambda service; any alternative ingress requires a separately bounded threat model.

Keep the one-second polling feature unless measurements show it is technically incompatible with the selected transport. Optimize payload shape/cache behavior before reducing useful liveness frequency.
Make routine live-card polling return only the data required by the card. Historical/task-wide data must not be retransmitted on every one-second poll if the UI does not need it.
Prove that ordinary Heartbeat MCP calls do not transmit unrelated ChatGPT conversation contents through the custom server; document exactly what data the server receives on routine tool/app calls.
Validate the new transport in isolation before replacing the current launcher/connection configuration. Preserve an operator-understandable rollback path until live ChatGPT acceptance passes.
After live acceptance, remove ngrok from the normal Heartbeat startup path and document whether any emergency fallback remains.
Do not modify GitRunner/self-hosted-control-plane authority, independent-review design, EXTRACT science, or unrelated workspace-control execution policy in this task.
constraints: This task is independent of workspace-github-actions-selfhosted-control-plane-v1 and may execute in parallel; do not mutate GitRunner design/code/task state.
Do not make the Lambda broadly internet-reachable merely to replace ngrok.
Do not assume Secure MCP Tunnel has unlimited bandwidth or specific quotas. Verify current official limits/capabilities before relying on them.
Do not infer the source of the 1.02 GB transfer solely from the one-second poll. Instrument/measure or bound the traffic first.
Do not remove the one-second liveness/card polling feature just because ngrok Free exhausted its quota; the feature is explicitly desired.
Do not conflate heartbeat_touch model calls with live-card/app snapshot polling. Identify each path separately and optimize the actual high-frequency path.
Do not reintroduce timed semantic Heartbeat noise. heartbeat_touch remains silent and semantic updates remain semantic-delta-driven.
Do not enable automatic stale-owner takeover or change lease/ownership semantics in this transport task.
Do not claim exact internal ChatGPT executor death is observable; preserve the accepted demonstrated-activity semantics.
Do not mutate the live runtime before exact repository/runtime provenance and rollback are recovered.
Any source/UI schema change must pass the existing Workspace Heartbeat tests and workspace-control validation before live deployment.
Durable task state in Git remains authoritative even while the Heartbeat MCP transport itself is unavailable.

notes:
Created 2026-10-26 after the operator identified the concrete cause of current Heartbeat connector failures: the free ngrok account exceeded its monthly network bandwidth allocation. The operator values the newly added executor-signal feature and reports that the card/server polls approximately once per second to show the latest executor signal. That feature is a requirement, not disposable overhead. The new task therefore treats transport and payload efficiency as the problem, not liveness semantics. Secure MCP Tunnel is the preferred direction if current official OpenAI support and limits are compatible. The task must empirically distinguish high-frequency live-card/app polling from heartbeat_touch model calls; do not assume they are the same traffic path. GitRunner work continues independently in its own task/chat.
